200 orders at a time, 2000 positions per day

Platform servers cap 200 simultaneous orders and 2000 max positions per day; an EA that overloads the server is warned and asked to adjust. A third-party EA used by other traders may be denied the account if it exceeds the maximum capital allocation rule. No stop loss required.

Expert advisors allowed within the Forbidden Trading Practices. The FAQ warns that a third-party EA shared with other traders can breach the maximum capital allocation rule, and that platform servers cap 200 orders at a time and 2000 positions per day.

exploiting price errors or update delays; opposite positions across accounts; gap trading (within 2 h of market close or around major macro events); ultra-high-speed tools or mass data entry; EAs over 2000 server requests per day; spreading profit to dodge the Best Day rule; disproportionate position sizes; third-party access

Summary of the Forbidden Trading Practices page. HFT, tick scalping, martingale, grid and copy trading are not named on it (only "ultra-high-speed tools" and EA request volume). The general FAQ requires strategies replicable on live and conforming to a real market.

News and overnight/weekend restrictions do not apply during the evaluation, whatever the account type.

Folder 'Prohibited Strategies/Practices' (6 articles, modified 13-14 May). HFT, arbitrage, grid, martingale and tick scalping are not named; scalping is defined by the 3-minute / 30 % profit test and the company may adjust or remove profits. Overleveraging articles give no numeric limit; the Risk Management Group article sets 3 % risked per trade (1 % Instant Lite) as 'all-or-nothing' trading, which cuts funded leverage (FX 1:30, indices/commodities 1:5, metals 1:3, crypto 1:1) — not applied to Challenge accounts.
